title: Rapid signal lanes — unscoped feedback + tactical asks (Apr 2027)
body:
Purpose: quick roll-up of high-frequency customer signals from Q1–Q2 2027 (unscoped: mix of hosted + dedicated + private).

One-liner summary:
- Customers repeatedly ask for two things: clearer model fallbacks + cheaper predictable throughput patterns. Many asks framed as operational risk mitigation.

Data sources used:
- Recent support threads (top 45 tickets tagged 'latency' or 'fallback')
- CS weekly call notes (Mar–Apr 2027)
- 6 post-onboarding check-ins with mid-market customers
- Quick survey sent to 22 customers (12 responses)

Raw/high-signal quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "When we hit spikes the app becomes unusable — we need a non-surprising fallback that keeps UX intact."
- "We can't explain why cost jumped one month — need per-route token breakdown in console that maps to features."
- "Quantized variants sometimes hallucinate more — want an A/B safety guard before switching in prod."

Top synthesized asks (ranked by signal frequency + CS severity):
1) Per-route cost & SLO dashboard (FR-9001) — customers want the ability to attribute token spend to routes/features and set soft SLO alerts. Impact: high. Effort: M. Suggested owner: product-hosted-api / observability. Related: Confluence page + JIRA-7182.
2) Controlled fallback lanes (FR-9002) — allow per-route fallback policies (model -> variant -> degrade-to-short-mode) with visible rollout metrics. Impact: high (prevents outages). Effort: L. Suggested owner: serving-runtime + console-and-rollouts. Prototype idea: UI toggles for 'graceful-fallback' with canned strategies.
3) Quantization safety gate (FR-9003) — automatic evaluation run when switching to quantized weights comparing quality delta on customer prompt set; rollback if regressions exceed threshold. Impact: medium-high. Effort: M. Suggested owner: applied-ml + optimize. Linked GH PR for eval harness.
4) Predictable reserved burst billing view (FR-9004) — customers on Dedicated want clearer burst vs commit billing breakdown and forecast controls. Impact: medium. Effort: S. Suggested owner: finance-and-legal + dedicated.
5) Faster trace sampling in high-traffic routes (FR-9005) — lower-latency sampling to surface cold-start events. Impact: medium. Effort: M. Suggested owner: observability + site-reliability-engineering.
6) Prompt-set-level regression alerts in Optimize (FR-9006) — tie evals to rollout policies; notify CS + customers on regressions. Impact: medium. Effort: M. Suggested owner: optimize + product-ops.

Quick cost vs impact cheat sheet (for planning chat):
- FR-9001 (dashboard): Medium cost, High impact — 30–45d dev + 2 engineers cross-team
- FR-9002 (fallback lanes): Larger infra change, High impact — 60–90d, requires runtime + console work
- FR-9003 (safety gate): Medium cost, Medium-High impact — 3–4 sprints for eval infra plus ML tests

Customer examples / micro-stories (for prioritization):
- Fintech startup (Dedicated): daily spikes from batch billing job, experienced 3x latency for 2 hours; fallback to smaller model would have kept critical flows online. Asks: explicit per-route fallback + canary tests.
- Marketplace (Hosted): monthly cost surprise due to a background job sending long-context prompts. Asks: per-route token billing + alerting.
- Health-tech (Private): regulatory need to avoid any external routing fallback; wants on-prem consistent behavior with deterministic quantization policies. Asks: private deploy config controls + verification report.

Open questions / unknowns we should answer before scoping:
- For per-route billing: how to reconcile with shared caches and KV reuse across routes? (tech question for serving-runtime).
- For fallbacks: do we allow model architecture mismatches (e.g., llama2 -> small-instruct) or only same-architecture variants?
- Quantization safety: what is an acceptable delta threshold per customer segment? (legal/regulatory customers may have stricter tolerance).

Immediate next steps (recommended sprint-level plan):
1) Triage meeting (CS + product-hosted-api + serving-runtime) — goal: agree on owner for FR-9001 + FR-9002 (target EOW).
2) Quick spike for per-route cost prototype — small console view using existing cost logs (2 wks).
3) Draft fallback policy UX copy — CS to draft 3 canned policies and example language for docs.
4) Add quantization safety gate as 'opt-in' MVP for early enterprise customers (pilot with 2 existing Private customers).

Suggested owners and immediate ask owners (names + contacts):
- FR-9001 owner candidate: Priya Kapoor (product-hosted-api) — priya@redwood.ai (CS asked to intro).
- FR-9002 owner candidate: Omar Haddad (serving-runtime) — ping on Slack #run-inference.
- FR-9003 owner candidate: Kelsey Ng (applied-ml) — has existing eval harness.

Notes on decision heuristics for PM prioritization (CS input):
- Any feature that prevents customer-visible downtime or an outage-like state gets >80% priority boost.
- Billing transparency features are high-conversion tools for upsell to Dedicated.
- Safety/regression tooling has strategic importance for Private customers; consider as enterprise-only pilot if resource-constrained.

Risks and mitigations:
- Big infra changes (fallbacks) could introduce complexity — mitigation: start with UI-only canary that triggers manual ops approval before automated fallbacks.
- Billing attribution may surface internal inconsistencies — mitigation: release as beta with strong caveats and CS-mediated rollout.

Appendix: short raw ticket excerpts (redacted):
- "Ticket 4521: sudden token cost spike, suspect background worker; customer wants per-route breakdown"
- "Ticket 4598: production latency spikes; asks for automatic fallback to smaller model or shorter max tokens"
- "Ticket 4629: hallucination increase after 8-bit switch; request: run our prompts through quantized variant before apply"
